title: Revocation (Experiment 5)
demonstrates: Revoking an artifact or a signing key invalidates it and everything derived from it, and the gateway blocks deployment; deleting index rows does not undo a revocation. Editing the trusted index itself is a documented limitation.

variants.title: Revoke the base model -> descendant fails
variants.attack: base model revoked; fine-tuned model verified

variants.title: Revoked ancestor -> deployment BLOCKED
variants.attack: gateway asked to deploy the fine-tuned model

variants.title: Revoke the training_pipeline key -> its models fail
evidence: V4 FAIL: key revoked at 2026-10-15T21:45:27.765009Z (training key compromised (simulated))

variants.title: Dataset signed by another role still verifies
variants.attack: same revocation of ed25519:4442de9d132b0e2e; dataset signed by data_steward

variants.title: Bypass: delete the revoked artifact's index row
variants.attack: revoked final model's row removed from the SQLite index
evidence: V7 FAIL: artifact not in registry index: revocation state cannot be confirmed

variants.title: Bypass: delete the revoked key from the trust store
variants.attack: revoked key ed25519:4442de9d132b0e2e row removed from the signers table
evidence: V3 FAIL: signing key ed25519:4442de9d132b0e2e is not in the trust store
V6 FAIL: parent digits-base-cnn FAILED (V3, V4)

variants.title: Bypass: overwrite cached status with VERIFIED
variants.attack: last_status column forced to VERIFIED for every artifact

variants.title: LIMITATION: un-revoke by editing the trusted index
variants.attack: revoked flag set back to 0 directly in SQLite

details.limitation: revocation state is stored in the trusted SQLite index; an attacker with write access to it can undo a revocation. Fix: signed append-only revocation list.

interpretation: Artifact and key revocation propagate to every descendant and block deployment. Deleting the revoked artifact or key from the index fails closed, and the cached status is never trusted. E5-C4 shows the remaining gap: the revocation flag itself is only as trustworthy as the index.
